text:
lee: Quick question for the group: we're designing the long-term egress strategy for Private deploys. Options on the table: ephemeral per-tenant IPs, shared regional gateway, or ENI-based per-tenant secondary IPs. Thoughts?

alex: ENI secondary IPs are interesting: attach an ENI per-tenant to a small egress fleet instance, you get stable IPs without EIP count explosion. But it couples us to ASG/instance lifecycle and cross-AZ routing gets fiddly.

maria: ENIs could help with BYOIP customers too. But managing thousands of ENIs may still hit account quotas and is operationally heavy. Need automation for attach/detach and failover.

sam: Ephemeral EIP pools vs shared gateway: shared gateway simplifies allocations and route tables but hides tenant identity. We could do per-tenant SNAT port ranges to reduce collision, but can't guarantee firewall-friendly stable IPs.

katie: Another idea: lightweight per-tenant reverse-proxy (SOCKS/http) that exits via shared gateway but preserves tenant metadata to downstream via a tenant-assertion header — only for customers that opt in to metadata sharing. For sensitive customers we give stable IPs.

lee: That metadata header leaks tenancy to 3rd-party endpoints — unacceptable for regulated customers. So we need a way to guarantee tenancy isolation for those cases.

alex: Right. So taxonomy: (A) full isolation: stable dedicated IP(s) (EIP/ENI/BYOIP) (B) soft-isolation: shared gateway + opaque proxy (no tenant id leaked) (C) shared: best-effort shared gateway for low-risk tenants.

maria: For (A) we should consider short/medium term: EIP allocation per-tenant, but with a pool manager that reuses IPs. Long-term: BYOIP prefix assignment for enterprise tenants to avoid cloud EIP limits.

sam: For (B), implement an application-proxy that terminates TLS to external endpoints on behalf of tenant, so external sees proxy IP but we can apply egress policies. Adds CPU cost and TLS ops.

katie: Cost estimates: proxy CPU + TLS handshakes will matter for heavy outbound workloads. ENI approach offloads NAT work to kernel but costs in instance footprint and cross-AZ bandwidth. Need a cost model matrix.

lee: Operational failure modes: ENI instance down -> tenant traffic must failover to another instance which may change source IPs. That breaks allowlists. So if we choose ENI, we need sticky failover (route reassign) or reserve standby IPs.

alex: Technical constraint: AWS doesn't allow ENI move across AZs; failover requires updating route target or using Transit Gateway attachments. More complex than EIP detach/attach.

maria: Telemetry: whichever design we pick must emit per-tenant egress metrics (bytes, flows, errors) and correlate with model-serving traces. Shared gateway needs tenant tagging upstream so we can aggregate correctly.

sam: Network policy enforcement: integrate with the agent so customers can opt-in denylists at the tenant level enforced at egress. Implementation varies by architecture though.

katie: Security-bot: reminder -> egress designs must preserve customer data plane confidentiality. Any header injection or proxy assertion should be opt-in and documented. Also require consent for PII leakage to third parties.

lee: Proposed decision approach: 1) Build a minimal EIP/ENI allocation manager spike (compare both on failure/recovery), 2) Prototype shared gateway + TLS-termination proxy and measure latency/CPU, 3) Produce cost/quotas spreadsheet and a risk matrix.

alex: I can take the shared gateway + proxy prototype. Will measure p95 latency, CPU, and TLS session reuse benefits.

maria: I'll own the EIP vs ENI spike and test failover semantics across AZs.

sam: I'll draft the telemetry + policy integration plan and the risk matrix.

katie: I'll prepare cost estimates and include BYOIP operational runbook notes.

security-bot: Note: log retention for egress flow records should be configurable per-tenant for compliance.

lee: Cool. Let's timebox spikes to 2 weeks and reconvene with data. If anyone finds related infra quotas or BYOIP contractual hurdles before then, ping the thread.
